node_definition.done_when: Read section 34 of crew-runtime-positive-controls and its comment c-crpc-s34-reverted first. Start by re-applying the reverted change as a patch, not a cherry-pick: run git diff 6ea9a15fa^1 6ea9a15fa, then git apply -3 on that output in your worktree, and commit it with a message saying it re-applies the reverted change. Then fix the regression. classify_pointer in reckon/crew/recovery.py must again read a completed run holding a parsed stored review as promotable when the run's record names no resolvable head, as it did at 6ea9a15fa^1, while an abbreviated commits: entry still resolves to its full id and never to the shared checkout's HEAD. Keep the refusal to compose a new review for a reclaimed run with no resolvable head; only stored-review selection for classification must not regress. Your gate includes tests/test_crew_scoring_state.py, tests/test_live_process_outranks_classification.py, tests/test_pointer_classification_is_memoised.py, tests/test_reclaimed_run_review_head.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py, tests/test_no_member_dispatch_runs_alone.py and tests/test_member_friction.py, plus any file grep finds for _review_head_and_tree, _run_head_for_review or _record_carried_head. The base arm at main must show the first three files passing, and the head arm must add no failure id. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/reclaimed-run-review-keys-on-its-own-head.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
